items.a: My work is integrative and context-oriented, which means I draw on several ways of working rather than following one fixed method. I bring together Systemic Counselling, Somatic Awareness, Parts Work and Mindfulness-Based Practice, and I shape our sessions around you as a person. The aim is always to meet you where you are and to work in a way that feels supportive and grounded.

items.q: Do you follow one method or several?
items.a: Several. Rather than applying a single technique, I weave together different approaches depending on what feels most helpful for you and your situation. This lets me stay flexible and responsive, so our work can adapt as your needs change over time.

Somatic Experiencing is a body-oriented way of working with stress and overwhelming experiences. It gently supports the nervous system toward greater regulation and a sense of grounding. By noticing what is happening in the body, we can create more ease, steadiness and choice. For a fuller introduction, you can read [what Somatic Experiencing is and how it helps with stress](/blog/what-is-somatic-experiencing).

Systemic counselling explores the relational and contextual patterns in your life and how they shape your experience. It looks at the connections between you and the people and environments around you, rather than viewing anything in isolation. This wider view often brings fresh understanding and new possibilities.

Parts work is a way of exploring the different parts of yourself with curiosity and compassion. We make space for the various inner voices and reactions you may carry, and meet them with kindness rather than judgement. This can help you feel more at ease with yourself and more whole.

I draw on Mindfulness-Based Practice to help you develop awareness of your thoughts and reactivity. As that awareness grows, it creates a little more space and, with it, more choice in how you respond. Over time this can bring a calmer, steadier relationship with everyday life.
